clue.text: Singer's Round 1 elimination — that's a surprise

indicators.note: eliminating something knocks it out, so one letter is dropped from the singer's name

parts.note: Boy George, lead singer of Culture Club
a round thing is the letter O, and the 1 says only the first of the two goes

explanation.surface: A singer is knocked out in the first round of a talent contest, to everyone's astonishment.
explanation.walkthrough: BOY GEORGE has two Os; only the first one goes, leaving BY GEORGE.
explanation.definitionFit: By George is an old-fashioned exclamation of astonishment, the same as saying that's a surprise.

clue.text: Hairy creature's sign of displeasure in bar

indicators.note: the jeer goes inside the prohibition word

parts.note: to bar is to ban
boo is jeered at something disliked

explanation.surface: A hairy animal shows its displeasure at being in a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bar' looks like a pub; it means prohibit.
explanation.definitionFit: A baboon is a large monkey with a shaggy coat, so a furry animal.

clue.text: Scandalous conclusion — Vlad getting thrown in cell!

indicators.note: the setter is thrown into the scandal ending, landing inside it

parts.note: -gate is the suffix tacked onto a scandal's name since Watergate
the setter's pseudonym, so the setter is me

explanation.surface: A scandal ends with the setter Vlad being thrown in a prison cell.
explanation.definitionFit: A gamete is a reproductive cell, such as a sperm or egg.

clue.text: Money transfer rejected in beginning

indicators.note: rejected means thrown back, so the word for the transfer reads upwards

parts.note: a giro is a bank or post office transfer of money, familiar in Britain
taken as written

explanation.surface: A payment is bounced back right at the start.
explanation.definitionFit: An origin is the source or starting point of something, so its beginning.

clue.text: Crack down hard over personnel to survive

indicators.note: the tough phrase goes over the department, holding it inside

parts.note: to get tough is to crack down hard
HR, human resources, is the personnel department

explanation.surface: A boss cracks down hard on staff to keep the firm alive.
explanation.definitionFit: To get through a hard time is to come out the other side of it, so to survive it.

clue.text: King fighting heartfelt rage over Duke?

indicators.note: letters that are fighting are thrown about in a scuffle, so they land in a new order

parts.note: taken as written, as the letters to mix

explanation.surface: A king, in a fit of heartfelt anger, goes to war over a duke's betrayal.
explanation.walkthrough: The Duke's D joins the thirteen letters of heartfelt rage in the mix; 'over' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Alfred the Great was the ninth-century Anglo-Saxon monarch of Wessex who resisted the Viking invasions.

clue.text: These could be Asian lot

indicators.note: could be says these letters could be rearranged into something else

parts.note: taken as written, as the letters to mix

explanation.surface: A group of people from Asia, described offhand.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the wordplay and the definition: the people of Laos are indeed an Asian lot.
explanation.definitionFit: Laotians are the people of Laos, a country in Southeast Asia, so a group of Asians.

clue.text: Telling disclosure — not against English

indicators.note: not says the abbreviations for against and English are dropped

parts.note: a revelation is a disclosure
V is versus

explanation.surface: A revealing disclosure is made, but not against England.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Telling' looks like an adjective meaning revealing; it is a noun, the act of telling a story.
explanation.definitionFit: A relation is a narrative or account, the act of relating a story.

clue.text: Topple the high flyer outside

indicators.note: the flyer goes outside, holding the mixed letters

parts.note: a drone is an unmanned aircraft

indicators.note: someone high is intoxicated, so the letters reel into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, as the letters to mix

explanation.surface: Bring down the high-flying person who is outside.
explanation.definitionFit: To dethrone is to remove a ruler or leader from power, so to topple them.

clue.text: Hit useless horse

parts.note: bum as an adjective means worthless or useless, as in a bum deal
a pinto is a piebald or spotted horse

explanation.surface: Someone strikes an animal that is no good for anything.
explanation.definitionFit: To bump into something is to collide with it, so it can stand for hit.

clue.text: Massage oil in bed — don't get so excited!

indicators.note: the reworked letters go inside the bed

parts.note: a cot is a small bed

indicators.note: massaging kneads and works something over, so the letters are kneaded into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, as the letters to mix

explanation.surface: A massage with oil in bed gets someone overheated, and they are told to calm down.
explanation.definitionFit: Cool it is an idiom telling someone to calm down and stop being agitated.

clue.text: Flat's unfashionable, I agree

parts.note: something that is out is no longer in fashion
Right! is a word of agreement

explanation.surface: Someone admits that their apartment is not stylish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flat' looks like a noun for an apartment; it is the adverb, as in a flat refusal.
explanation.definitionFit: A flat refusal is an outright one: both mean complete and unqualified.

clue.text: Regrets I may harbour over man

indicators.note: over in a down-or-across sense means turned back, read backwards
to harbour is to hold within, so the letters sit inside these words

parts.note: the run of letters sits across these three words

explanation.surface: Someone admits there may be regrets that they keep hidden, over a man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'harbour' takes RETSIM from regRETS I May; 'over' then turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Mister is the title or form of address for a man, used informally as a noun for him.

clue.text: Eastern doctor working at sharp end displays a fuller figure

parts.note: MB is Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor's degree
a machine that is on is working
a point is the sharp end of a blade or pin

explanation.surface: An Eastern doctor working at the sharp end of medicine is putting on weight.
explanation.definitionFit: Embonpoint, borrowed from French, is a polite word for plumpness, a well-rounded body.

clue.text: Shared love admitted by veiled lady — it isn't proper!

parts.note: something common is held jointly or shared

indicators.note: being admitted, the zero goes inside the religious woman

parts.note: a nun wears a veil
love is nil in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: A nun lets slip that she shares a love with someone, which would be quite improper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Proper' is grammar: a proper noun names a particular thing, so the opposite kind is not proper.
explanation.definitionFit: Grammar contrasts proper nouns, names like London, with general ones like city.

clue.text: See 5
At first, dirty old man's uplifted during rarely clean entertainment

indicators.note: during puts the lifted letters in the middle of the mixed ones
rarely, cooked rare, says the letters are worked over into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, as the letters to mix

indicators.note: uplifted in a down clue means read from bottom to top
at first means only the opening letter of dirty

parts.note: its first letter only
pa is father, one's old man

explanation.surface: A dirty old man gets excited at a show that is seldom wholesome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rarely clean' reads as a judgement on the show, but rarely is the signal to rework clean.
explanation.definitionFit: A lap dance is an erotic dance performed close to a seated customer in a strip club, a kind of show.

clue.text: He's a fount of knowledge? Group of ladies crease up

parts.note: the WI, the Women's Institute, is a British women's organisation

indicators.note: letters that are up are stirred up, rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, as the letters to mix

explanation.surface: A know-all makes a women's group crease up with laughter.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks irony: a wiseacre only thinks he knows everything.
explanation.definitionFit: A wiseacre is a know-all, someone who pretends to great wisdom.

clue.text: Lab assistant?

definitions.meaning: reads as a laboratory, but is a Labrador retriever
a dog trained to help a deaf owner by alerting them to sounds

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a technician in a science laboratory; the Lab is the breed of dog, often trained to help deaf people.
explanation.definitionFit: Such a dog is trained to alert a deaf person to doorbells, alarms and other sounds.

clue.text: Plaster over gashes used up, Charlie gathered

indicators.note: the reversed letters gather Charlie inside them
up in a down clue means written from bottom to top

parts.note: O is the cricket scorer's abbreviation for an over
cuts are gashes
C in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Plaster applied over wounds, with Charlie collecting the used supplies.
explanation.definitionFit: Stucco is a fine plaster used to coat walls or make mouldings.

clue.text: Extra posh bloke? Quite

parts.note: a nob is an upper-class person
all means quite, completely, as in all alone

explanation.surface: An extra posh man is asked if he is quite so.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, a no-ball is an illegal delivery that gives the batting side an extra run.
explanation.definitionFit: Runs not scored off the bat are called extras in cricket, and a no-ball is one kind.

clue.text: Wound in side originally not dressed

indicators.note: originally takes just the first letter of side

parts.note: its first letter only
naked means without clothes

explanation.surface: An injury in the side is left unbandaged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wound' looks like an injury; it is the past tense of wind, to twist.
explanation.definitionFit: A road that snaked twisted and turned, as if winding along.

clue.text: Though not large, pleased to be given something handy

indicators.note: not large means the letter for large is left out

parts.note: glad means pleased
to get something is to be given it

explanation.surface: Someone is pleased to receive a present even though it is small.
explanation.definitionFit: A gadget is a small handy device or tool, something useful to have about.

clue.text: Describing time travelling options, here's Hawking

definitions.note: hawking means clearing the throat noisily and spitting

indicators.note: to describe a circle is to draw around, so the shuffled letters go round the time
letters that are travelling move about, so they settle into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, as the letters to mix

explanation.surface: A clue that seems to be about Stephen Hawking and his ideas on travelling in time.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface points to the physicist Stephen Hawking; here hawking is spitting, and a spittoon is where that goes.
explanation.definitionFit: A spittoon is a receptacle for spit, so it is the place where hawking and spitting is done.

clue.text: Presumably she wouldn't have voted for Brexit

definitions.meaning: a woman, so the answer is a girl's name
she would have found the European Union nice, so wanted to stay in it

explanation.walkthrough: The name splits as EU plus NICE: a woman who thinks the European Union is nice would hardly vote to leave it.
explanation.definitionFit: Eunice is a female first name, and read in two parts it praises the European Union.

clue.text: Initially Guardian setter's brilliant (or inferior?)

indicators.note: initially means only the first letter of the newspaper's name is used

parts.note: its first letter only
the setter refers to himself as I, so setter's is I'm, I am
crack means first-rate, as in a crack shot

explanation.surface: The Guardian setter wonders whether he is brilliant or not much good.
explanation.definitionFit: Gimcrack describes something showy but flimsy and poorly made, so cheap and of low quality.

clue.text: Force under pressure males on drugs to stop dangerous races

indicators.note: to stop up a gap is to plug it, so these letters fill the gap inside the races

parts.note: the TT races are motorbike races on the Isle of Man, notoriously dangerous
two males: he, a male pronoun, and M, the abbreviation for male
E is ecstasy

explanation.surface: Police under pressure stop drugged men from taking part in risky road races.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Males' is plural, so it supplies two male markers, HE and M; 'under pressure' is part of the surface picture.
explanation.definitionFit: The Met is the Metropolitan Police, London's police force.

clue.text: Had constitutional crisis finally — rang to get Queen involved

indicators.note: finally means just the closing letter of the word crisis is taken

parts.note: its last letter only

indicators.note: the Queen gets involved, wrapped up inside the bell-ringing word

parts.note: a bell that tolled rang
R is Regina, Latin for queen

explanation.surface: A constitutional crisis is reached when bells ring and the monarch must step in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Constitutional' suggests a political crisis; a constitutional is also a walk taken for health.
explanation.definitionFit: To take a constitutional is to go for a health-giving walk, so having had one is to have walked leisurely.
